tldr: This is a theme thread, not one event: six November items share the words "policy learning" or "policy improvement" across speech translation, multi-agent orchestration, robotics, and continual RL. Google's Gemini 4 Argon, framed partly around robot policy improvement, is the only product release in the set.
whats_new: CO-GRAFT (Nov 23) swaps RL-trained and pre-RL policies role by role in Search-R1 agents and finds query generation accounts for at most 15% of the RL gain.
why_it_matters: For agent builders, the useful strand is attribution: knowing which agent role RL actually improved tells you where to spend fine-tuning and eval effort.

beats.headline: RL-style policy learning applied to speech translation and agent orchestration
beats.summary: Two arXiv papers treat a latency trade-off and an orchestrator's agent selection as learned policies.

beats.headline: Google ships Gemini 4 Argon for robot control and policy improvement
Continual-RL replay and zero-shot advantage features
beats.summary: Two general RL methods papers with no agent-system deployment yet.

beats.headline: CO-GRAFT attributes search-agent RL gains to individual roles

open_questions: Does CO-GRAFT's role-level attribution hold for agents beyond Search-R1?
If query generation explains at most 15% of the gain, which role explains the rest?
Will any learned-orchestration method ship in an open-source agent framework?
take_for_builders: Before RL-tuning a whole search agent, ablate per role (query writing, reading, answering) to find which step the training actually improves.
